As with `bindConstructor`, `process()` only calls `handleJavaBeanProperties` when `beanInfo != null`, but NullAway doesn’t track that. I’ll add a local null guard at the start of `handleJavaBeanProperties`, which is behavior-preserving and should clear this new error without affecting others. Then I’ll rerun the compile to confirm the total error count drops from 83 to 82.

```bash
cd /home/vscode/nullness-benchmarks/spring-boot && sed -i '161,167s/private void handleJavaBeanProperties(ReflectionHints hints) {/private void handleJavaBeanProperties(ReflectionHints hints) {\n\t\t\tif (this.beanInfo == null) {\n\t\t\t\treturn;\n\t\t\t}/' spring-boot-project/spring-boot/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/context/properties/bind/BindableRuntimeHintsRegistrar.java && ./gradlew :spring-boot-project:spring-boot:compileJava -x test -q > new_build_output.log 2>&1 && grep -n "BindableRuntimeHintsRegistrar" new_build_output.log || grep -n "errors" new_build_output.log | tail -n 5
```
